Palladium-Catalyzed Intermolecular Allenylation Reactions of 2,3-
Disubstituted Indoles and Allenyl Carbonate 
Yizhan Zhai,a,b Shu-Li You,*a,b and Shengming Ma*a,c 
A palladium-catalyzed intermolecular allenylation of non-strained 
2,3-disubstituted indoles and allenyl carbonate has been 
developed, providing a convenient access to indolenines bearing 
an allene unit by taking advantage of the C-3 nucleophilicity of 
indoles. Decent yields and good functional group tolerance have 
been achieved with diverse indoles under mild conditions. Gram-
scale reaction and various synthetic transformations have been 
demonstrated. 
Allenes are an important class of compounds in chemical 
transformation1 and natural product synthesis.2 Functionaliza-
tion of allenes is also an important means to access to allene 
containing various structure.3 On the other hand, indoles are 
intriguing and pivotal structural motifs in numerous natural 
products and pharmaceuticals.4 The studies on utilizing the 
nucleophilicity of C-3 of indoles to synthesize indolenines has 
made a great progress in recent years.5 However, such a C3-
allenylation of indoles has not been well established: the only 
example is the reaction of strained 1,2,3,4,5-
tetrahydrocyclopta-[b]indole.5m Here we wish to report a 
general solution for the C3-allenylation of the non-strained 
indoles with high efficiency.
     Initially, we employed 2,3-dimethyl-indole 1a6a with a very 
low reactivity and buta-2, 3-dienyl methyl carbonate 2a7 as the 
standard substrates to explore the optimal conditions for this 
allenylation reaction. Fortunately, the expected product 3a 
was observed in 18% yield in DCM in the presence of t-BuOK, 
Et3B,5e Pd2(dba)3, and DEPhos at room temperature (Table 1, 
entry 1). When t-BuOK was replaced with NaOMe and NaH, 
the reaction gave poorer results (Table 1, entries 2 and 3). 
Increasing the dosage of t-BuOK did not help (Table 1, entry 4). 
When 2 equiv. of Et 3B were used, there was a noteworthy 
improvement (Table 1, entry 5). Further experimental results on 
solvent screening revealed that DCM and MTBE gave the best 
performance (Table 1, entries 5-10). Owing to better solubility of 
reactants in DCM, we chose it as solvent for further optimization. 
We then screened the different leaving groups of the allene 
substrates. There were remarkable improvements when OAc (2b), 
OBz (2c), and OBoc (2d) were served as leaving groups (Table 1, 
entries 11-13) with OBoc being the best. Employing 1.5 equiv. of 2d 
could bring a slight enhancement (Table 1, entry 14). There was a 
decline when we continued to improve the amount of 2d (Table 1, 
entry 15). With this set of optimized reaction conditions, the 1 
mmol scale reaction could give a satisfactory result (Table 1, entry 
16).
     With the optimized reaction conditions in hand, we started to 
examine the scope of the reaction by applying various indoles. 
Different substitutions at C-5 of indole, such as F, Cl, Br, Me, MeO, 
are compatible, giving the corresponding allenylation products 3b-
3f in decent yields (Table 2, entries 1-5). Benzyl and ester groups 
could be tolerated at the C-3 position of indole (Table 2, entries 6 
and 7).
Furthermore, we turned our attentions to using 2-non-methyl-
substituted 2,3-disubstituted indoles. For 2-ethyl-3-methylindole 
and different non-strained hydrocycloalk[ b]indoles, the reaction 
proceeded smoothly. It is worth mentioning that ketal ( 1m)6b is also 
compatible well.  As a comparison, the reaction of substrate bearing 
a ketone unit 1n afforded the related impure product 3n just in 27% 
yield with 34% recovery of the starting material. The reaction of 
tetracyclic 1o under the standard conditions also afforded the 
related product 3o, which is not stable during purification by silica 
gel column chromatography. Thus, reduction was carried out to 
generate corresponding indoline cis-4 (Scheme 1).8

     The reaction was successfully conducted on 6 mmol scale of 1j, 
affording 3j in 96% yield. The copper-catalyzed borylcuprations of 
allenes with bis(pinacolato)diboron generated vinylboronates 
product 5 with a high regio- and stereoselectivity. 9 The product of 
cis-fused tetrahydrocarbazole bearing a terminal allene unit cis-6 
could be obtained by reacting with organolithium reagents. 10 Linear 
(Z)-allylsilanes 7 could be synthesized through cobalt-catalyzed 
allene-hydrosilylation method with a high regio- and 
stereoselectivity.11 The compound 3j could also easily react with 
acetyl chloride generating enamine 8 (Scheme 2).

Conclusions
In summary, a general palladium-catalyzed intermolecular 
allenylation of non-strained 2,3-disubstituted indoles with 2,3-
allenyl carbonate was  developed affording functionalized C3-
allene-substituted indolines via N-indolyltriethylborates. The 
reaction has exhibited good yields and a broad substrate scope 
under mild conditions. The products have been demonstrated to 
undergo some synthetically useful transformations. Further studies 
the reaction is ongoing in our laboratory.
